text:
Let us adore ivory flesh,

let us gild faces of archaic profiles,

aristocratic treasure;

foreheads bathed in pale gold,

hands with elongated phalanges,

where noble blood runs blue.


Come, let us adore

the arcane Ideal, companions.


Let us adore dilated eyes,

steeped, like a sea of shadows,

in diaphanous and astral clarities,

eyes that hysteria brightens,

eyes that by day are abyss,

eyes that by night are beacons.


Come, let us adore

the arcane Ideal, companions.


Let us adore souls forever aloof,

the most silent, the strange,

that never dissolve into loves:

urn-souls of immense desolations,

that rise intact to the heavens,

or sink intact into Cocytus.


Come, let us adore

the arcane Ideal, companions.


O poets, exalted lovers

of the arcane Ideal, rulers

of rebellious form: let us labor

to rebuild the Gothic altars,

and then to their protective shadows

come, let us adore!

translation.title: Let Us Adore the Ivory Flesh...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the incantatory refrain and the poem’s decadent catalogue of the arcane Ideal.
